Leonardo, this is Marion Delacroix, general counsel at Northgate Pay. I have read the file note your team sent, and I would like to move our call to Thursday, because I want my chief financial officer on it. Two things before we speak. First, do not walk me through the history. I know the history. I need to hear where we stand today and what you recommend. Second, when you get to the two scenarios, give me numbers, not adjectives. If the ruling is granted, what does that do to our cash position this year, and if it is refused, what does the restructuring actually cost. My chief financial officer will interrupt you, and he will ask you to elaborate on anything that sounds vague, so be ready to clarify without going back to the beginning. One last thing, and I mean it kindly. You have been on this file since March. You know it better than anyone in this building. Speak like it.

I want to tell you what changes at the halfway point, because it is not what people expect. At the beginning you are collecting things. Words, structures, a way to build a conditional, a way to describe a rule without naming anyone. You are filling a box. And then one day somebody asks you a question in a meeting, and you do not go to the box at all. The sentence just comes out, and afterwards you cannot remember which rule you used. That is the moment the language stops being homework. But something else happens at the same time, and nobody warns you about it. You start to hear your own mistakes while you are still speaking. That is uncomfortable, and most people react by slowing down and getting quieter, which is exactly the wrong move. The right move is to correct yourself in three words and keep going. Let me rephrase that. What I mean is this. Sorry, the rate is fifteen, not fifty. Nobody in that room thinks less of you. What they notice is that you did not stop.

Thank you for making the time. Let me articulate where the file stands today. We have advised the group since March, and the exposure has grown since the acquisition. If the ruling is granted this quarter, the rate falls to ten percent. My recommendation is that we file the restructuring plan before December.
